chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy the sheep, or a group buys the sheep, then they are brought into a house, then a man stands at the door and counts one, two, three, four, and five, then he draws the lot.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not valid. The lots are only valid if the distribution is just.'

key_terms.السَّهْم: Lot or share drawn by chance

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of drawing lots in partnership distribution?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of *qur'ah* (drawing lots) is contingent upon the equity of the underlying division, not merely the mechanical act of selection. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that procedural fairness must be rooted in substantive justice, ensuring that chance does not mask an unfair distribution of assets among partners.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umer, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Minhal Al Qassab who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I buy the sheep, or a group buys the sheep, then they enter a house, then a man stands upon the door, so he number one, and two, and three, and four, and five, then he specifies it as one share’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is not correct. But rather shares are correct only when distribution is just’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Minhal al-Qassab who has said the following: “

This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of my buying sheep or a group’s buying sheep saying, ‘They enter a house, then a man stands at the door counts one, two, three, four, and five, then calls it one share.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not valid. Shares are valid only when they are equal.’”
